defects.summary: APlanWithFlags_IsRefusedForKimi tests only a plan with Flags, but MustCarryNoFlags also refuses Leading and AddDirs, and no test covers those two arms.
The junction-first tests assert only that the deleter's recorder stayed empty; nothing proves that KimiHome actually unlinked a junction (only that a shim with --home was launched).
The new 'Kimi's arm (E5.6, 2026-10-13)' paragraph dates the build with the measurement day, but the work is dated 2026-10-25 in module_tests.md and in the plan.

W.summary: All the product decisions are correct: the planner arm, no flags, a refusal that covers Flags, Leading and AddDirs, the rows with the right cells and date, the vectors, the generated table and the Records entry. The tests reuse the existing Adapters() entry, and S5.6.7 adds a launch-control arm that proves the home existed when the refusal came. The module docs (core, runners, tests) and the plan's deviations are updated with care.

defects.summary: The refused arm of S5.6.7 compares the coai-question-* folders in the global TEMP before and after the ask, which the author admits another test could disturb.
The failing arm of S5.5.2 asserts only that state is not 'answered' instead of 'failed', and the cancelled arm of S5.6.7 accepts either a throw or a reply.
The tests build a second KimiConsultant although Adapters() already holds one, the Scopes helper is copied into two files, and a local OneShotFolder const repeats VibeHomes.OneShotFolder.
Properties are named _data and _temp, in the field naming style.
This file is not updated and still says the kimi disk standing 'will be unconfined (S5)'.

X.summary: The product change matches W's, and the refusal covers all three plan fields, with a Theory over each. Its tests have the strongest proof of junction-first disposal: they also assert that KimiHome unlinked once. But some assertions are looser, the helpers are copied, and one doc is stale.

defects.summary: It rewrites the shared Unconfined caveat in the C# code and in its twin in capabilityAdmission.ts, for every unconfined runtime (codex included). This is outside E5.5/E5.6, against the spec's 'as codex's none does', and it is not recorded as a deviation.
The launch-refused arm asserts only that one version probe ran, not that the owned home and its junction existed when the refusal came.
S5.6.6 tests only a plan with Flags, but the code also refuses Leading and AddDirs.
No research/module_*.md file is updated for the new rows, the planner arm or the tests, though the epic's DoD asks for it.
It removes the blank line between two members, against the file's style.

Y.summary: The required product change is correct and complete, and moving the Adapters() Kimi entry into a helper is good reuse. S5.6.7 has a clean Version seam for a launch-control refusal. But an unrequested change to user-facing text for all unconfined runtimes, with no recorded deviation, lowers it.

defects.summary: MustCarryNoFlags refuses Flags and Leading but not AddDirs, so a plan that carries --add-dir roots is still built, against decision 3's 'ANY flag'.
Deviation 56 says the S5.5.3 test catches OperationCanceledException and does not assert the ending, but the test has no catch and asserts state failed with failureKind cancelled.
S5.5.5 and S5.6.6 are in a new class outside the classes the spec names, and it copies the fixtures of ConfinementPlannerTests (RootA/B, RowFolder, Plan, Planned).
TheHomesFolderIsEmpty passes without a check if coai-vh does not exist, and the AGENTS.md and .kimi-code fixtures are written but nothing asserts on them.
S5.5.4 does not assert that the check passed and uses the literal 'own' instead of ConsultantCheck.OwnName; the Scopes helper is copied into two files.

Z.summary: The rows, the vectors, the planner arm and the generated table are correct. But the flag refusal misses AddDirs, and one recorded deviation describes a test that does not exist in that form. The tests repeat fixtures in a new class, and some assertions can pass without checking anything.

reasoning: All four pass every objective check and have the same planner arm, rows, vectors and table, so the ranking comes from the edges. W and X both refuse all three plan fields and update the docs; W reuses the code better and adds a better-proved launch-control arm, and X's stronger junction proof does not make up for its copied helpers and looser assertions. Y loses for its unrequested and unrecorded change to the shared caveat, and Z loses for the missing AddDirs refusal, a false deviation record and copied test fixtures.
